purpose: Measure kq's own capacity ceiling on the north-star execution-time distribution with a minimal load generator that removes kq-bench's per-event JSON and Python accounting overhead, and measure the Kafka cost of concurrent versus serial Enqueue.
runner: probe/main.go (kq.Client and kq.Worker used unmodified); probe/run.sh
command: probe/run.sh <label> <rps> <duration> <partitions> <worker processes> <workers per process> <concurrency> <producer clients> <goroutines per client>

topology.notes: Per-point partitions, worker processes, workers per process, concurrency, and producer clients are recorded in result.json. max_retries=0, so no retry topics or movers.

execution_time_ms.distribution: lognormal, sigma=ln(646/475)/(2.326-1.645), mean 250 ms, seeded by task ID

notes: One run per point. Kafka is bench/compose.yaml (one broker, RF=1), recreated per point. Workers started 12 s before producers; the share group used share.auto.offset.reset=earliest. Queue time is handler start minus the producer timestamp taken immediately before Enqueue. Correctness counts unique completed task IDs across all worker processes.
